title: Charge-Coupled Device-Based Arbitrary Waveform Generation for Qubit Control
abstract: We propose an arbitrary waveform generation architecture based on charge-coupled devices (CCDs) for qubit control. Waveform samples are stored as charge packets in CCD channels and sequentially clocked out as voltage samples. Multiple channels are operated in parallel and time-interleaved to achieve high effective sampling rates. The generated baseband waveforms are then upconverted to microwave frequencies to drive qubit operations. By representing waveform information as stored charge rather than as continuously generated or transmitted microwave signals, the proposed architecture provides a path to reducing cryogenic interconnect density and lowering heat load in scalable quantum control systems.
summary: This paper proposes using Charge-Coupled Devices (CCDs) to generate arbitrary microwave waveforms for qubit control. Instead of continuous microwave transmission, the method stores waveform data as charge, which is read out and upconverted. This approach significantly reduces the heat load and interconnect density required inside dilution refrigerators, enabling scalable quantum control systems.
main_problem: Delivering accurately calibrated microwave waveforms to a large number of qubits in a cryogenic environment presents a major engineering challenge due to interconnect density and heat load.
main_result: The proposed CCD-based architecture significantly reduces the required cryogenic heat load by storing waveform information as charge rather than continuously generating microwave signals.
method: The method involves storing digital waveform samples as charge packets in CCD channels, reading them out sequentially as baseband voltage, and then upconverting this signal to the required microwave frequency.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting quantum processor requiring precise microwave control signals. The proposed solution utilizes Charge-Coupled Devices (CCDs) as a non-continuous, charge-storage medium for waveform generation.
key_observables: Effective sampling rates (up to $MN$ sps), required power for transfer clocks ($P_{clk}$), and resulting cryogenic heat load ($\alpha P_{clk}$).
important_parameters: Target capacitance ($C = 1 	ext{ pF}$), operating voltage ($V = 3.3 	ext{ V}$), and the heat load fraction ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The reference power calculation uses a commercial CCD, and the feasibility relies on achieving a low target capacitance ($C = 1 	ext{ pF}$) in a purpose-built CCD structure at cryogenic temperatures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the overall proposed CCD-based architecture for qubit control, while Figure 2 details the operational phases: waveform loading (writing charge) and waveform output (reading charge).
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the engineering bottleneck (heat load from continuous signal generation). It then proposes the CCD store-and-readout paradigm. The core of the work involves calculating the power requirements, comparing a reference CCD estimate to an optimized, low-capacitance estimate, and concluding with the architectural advantage.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical implementation challenges of scaling quantum processors by proposing a novel, low-heat-load classical control interface, which is crucial for realizing large-scale quantum computation.
